shared.concept_anchor: Mathura as religious melting pot under Kushana patronage

en.display_text:
Consider the following Assertion (a) and Reason (R):

Assertion (a): The Mathura school of sculpture is unique in Indian art history for simultaneously producing significant sculptural traditions for Buddhism, Jainism, and Hinduism within the same geographic location and broadly contemporaneous period.

Reason (R): Mathura's position at the convergence of major overland trade routes made it one of ancient India's most cosmopolitan urban centres, attracting devotees, merchants, monks, and artisans from communities of multiple faiths.

Which of the following is correct?

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: b — Students who verify A and R as both correct may second-guess whether the causal link is direct enough — the connection between Mathura's trade-route location and its multi-religious sculptural output is genuine but slightly indirect, making option (b) a plausible alternative for careful but uncertain students.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is A correct? Yes — the Mathura school uniquely produced Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu sculptural traditions simultaneously from the same workshops and in the same historical period.

Step 2: Is R correct? Yes — Mathura's location at the convergence of major trade routes (Uttarapatha, Dakshinapatha connections) made it a hub for merchants, pilgrims, and communities of multiple faiths.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? Yes — Mathura's role as a trade and pilgrimage crossroads directly explains why it attracted devotees, donors, and artisans from Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu communities, producing patronage for all three traditions simultaneously.
Both A and R correct, R explains A → option (a).
en.final_explanation:
Mathura's unique character as a multi-religious sculptural center is explained by its geographic and economic position.

Assertion (a): Correct. Mathura is distinctive in Indian art history for simultaneously producing major sculptural traditions for all three of India's great institutional religions — Buddhism, Jainism, and Hinduism — within the same workshops and historical period. Buddhist stupas and Bodhisattva images, Jain Tirthankara figures and Ayagapatas, and early Hindu images of Vishnu, Shiva, and Krishna were all produced at Mathura.

Reason (R): Correct. Mathura's geographic position at the junction of major trade arteries — including the Uttarapatha (northern highway connecting the northwest to eastern India) and routes connecting the Gangetic plain to western and southern India — made it one of ancient India's most cosmopolitan urban centers. Merchants, pilgrims, monks, and artisans from multiple religious communities converged there.

Causal relationship: R directly and sufficiently explains A. The convergence of multiple religious communities at Mathura — enabled by its trade-route crossroads location — created patronage demand for Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu art simultaneously. Without this geographic-commercial factor, the multi-religious character of Mathura's output would be inexplicable.

Value Addition:
• Mathura's position on the Uttarapatha also explains why Kushana rulers — who controlled the silk road trade — chose it as their southern capital.
• The same trade-route logic explains Nalanda's rise as a multi-disciplinary Buddhist university — it too was situated on a major trade corridor.
• Krishna's mythological birthplace identity added a specifically Hindu devotional overlay to Mathura's already pluralistic religious landscape.

hi.display_text:
निम्नलिखित कथन (a) और कारण (R) पर विचार करें:

कथन (a): मथुरा की मूर्तिकला परंपरा भारतीय कला इतिहास में अद्वितीय है क्योंकि यह एक ही भौगोलिक स्थान और लगभग समकालीन काल में बौद्ध धर्म, जैन धर्म, और हिंदू धर्म के लिए महत्वपूर्ण मूर्तिकला परंपराओं का एक साथ उत्पादन करती है।

कारण (R): मथुरा की स्थिति प्रमुख स्थलीय व्यापार मार्गों के संगम पर होने के कारण यह प्राचीन भारत के सबसे वैश्विक शहरी केंद्रों में से एक था, जो विभिन्न धार्मिक समुदायों के भक्तों, व्यापारियों, संन्यासियों और कारीगरों को आकर्षित करता था।

निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सही है?

(a) A और R दोनों सही हैं, और R, A का सही स्पष्टीकरण है
(b) A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A का सही स्पष्टीकरण नहीं है
(c) A सही है लेकिन R गलत है
(d) A गलत है लेकिन R सही है
hi.strong_distractor: b — जो छात्र A और R दोनों को सही मानते हैं, वे यह संदेह कर सकते हैं कि क्या कारणात्मक संबंध पर्याप्त रूप से प्रत्यक्ष है — मथुरा के व्यापार मार्ग की स्थिति और इसके बहुधार्मिक मूर्तिकला उत्पादन के बीच संबंध वास्तविक है लेकिन थोड़ा अप्रत्यक्ष है, जिससे विकल्प (b) सावधान लेकिन अनिश्चित छात्रों के लिए एक संभावित विकल्प बन जाता है।
elimination_logic: चरण 1: क्या A सही है? हाँ — मथुरा स्कूल ने अद्वितीय रूप से एक ही कार्यशालाओं और एक ही ऐतिहासिक काल में बौद्ध, जैन और हिंदू मूर्तिकला परंपराओं का एक साथ उत्पादन किया।
चरण 2: क्या R सही है? हाँ — मथुरा की स्थिति प्रमुख व्यापार मार्गों (उत्तरपथ, दक्षिणपथ कनेक्शन) के संगम पर थी, जिसने इसे व्यापारियों, तीर्थयात्रियों और विभिन्न धार्मिक समुदायों के लिए केंद्र बना दिया।

चरण 3: क्या R, A को कारणात्मक रूप से समझाता है? हाँ — मथुरा का व्यापार और तीर्थयात्रा के चौराहे के रूप में स्थान सीधे यह समझाता है कि क्यों यह बौद्ध, जैन और हिंदू समुदायों के भक्तों, दाताओं और कारीगरों को आकर्षित करता था, जिससे तीनों परंपराओं के लिए संरक्षण एक साथ उत्पन्न हुआ।
A और R दोनों सही हैं, और R, A को समझाता है → विकल्प (a)।
hi.final_explanation:
मथुरा की बहुधार्मिक मूर्तिकला केंद्र के रूप में विशिष्टता उसकी भौगोलिक और आर्थिक स्थिति से समझाई जाती है।

कथन (a): सही। मथुरा भारतीय कला इतिहास में विशिष्ट है क्योंकि यह एक ही कार्यशालाओं और ऐतिहासिक काल में भारत के तीन प्रमुख संस्थागत धर्मों — बौद्ध धर्म, जैन धर्म, और हिंदू धर्म — के लिए महत्वपूर्ण मूर्तिकला परंपराओं का एक साथ उत्पादन करता है। बौद्ध स्तूप और बोधिसत्त्व की प्रतिमाएँ, जैन तीर्थंकर आकृतियाँ और अयागपात, तथा प्रारंभिक हिंदू विष्णु, शिव और कृष्ण की प्रतिमाएँ सभी मथुरा में निर्मित हुईं।

कारण (R): सही। मथुरा की भौगोलिक स्थिति प्रमुख व्यापार मार्गों के संगम पर है — जिसमें उत्तरपथ (उत्तर-पश्चिम से पूर्वी भारत को जोड़ने वाला मुख्य मार्ग) और गंगा मैदान को पश्चिमी और दक्षिणी भारत से जोड़ने वाले मार्ग शामिल हैं — जिसने इसे प्राचीन भारत के सबसे वैश्विक शहरी केंद्रों में से एक बना दिया। व्यापारी, तीर्थयात्री, संन्यासी और कारीगर विभिन्न धार्मिक समुदायों से यहाँ एकत्रित होते थे।

कारणात्मक संबंध: R सीधे और पर्याप्त रूप से A को समझाता है। मथुरा में विभिन्न धार्मिक समुदायों का संगम — जो इसके व्यापार मार्गों के चौराहे के कारण संभव हुआ — ने बौद्ध, जैन और हिंदू कला के लिए एक साथ संरक्षण की मांग उत्पन्न की। यदि यह भौगोलिक-व्यापारिक कारक न होता, तो मथुरा के बहुधार्मिक चरित्र को समझाना असंभव होता।

Value Addition:
• मथुरा की उत्तरपथ पर स्थिति यह भी समझाती है कि क्यों कुषाण शासकों ने, जो रेशम मार्ग व्यापार को नियंत्रित करते थे, इसे अपनी दक्षिणी राजधानी चुना।
• वही व्यापार मार्ग तर्क नालंदा के बहुविषयक बौद्ध विश्वविद्यालय के रूप में उदय को भी समझाता है — वह भी एक प्रमुख व्यापार गलियारे पर स्थित था।
• कृष्ण के पौराणिक जन्मस्थान की पहचान ने मथुरा के पहले से ही बहुधार्मिक धार्मिक परिदृश्य पर एक विशिष्ट हिंदू भक्तिपूर्ण परत जोड़ी।

Consider the following statements regarding the Gupta period and its relationship to the Mathura school:

1. Compared to the Kushana-period Mathura style, the Gupta-period Mathura Buddha shows a more serene facial expression, greater refinement of drapery, and floral motifs in the halo — reflecting a shift from physical robustness to spiritual idealization.
2. The Sarnath Gupta Buddha and the Mathura Gupta Buddha are stylistically indistinguishable, representing a unified 'Gupta imperial style' that erased all regional differences between the two centers.
3. Both the Mathura and Gandhara schools reached their artistic peak under Kushana patronage, and both declined simultaneously following the fall of the Kushana Empire in the 3rd century CE.

Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?

(a) 1 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 2 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Compared to the Kushana-period Mathura style, the Gupta-period Mathura Buddha shows a more serene facial expression, greater refinement of drapery, and floral motifs in the halo — reflecting a shift from physical robustness to spiritual idealization.
statement_analysis.reason: This accurately describes the Kushana-to-Gupta stylistic transition at Mathura: from the powerful, sensuous Kushana Buddha to the more spiritually refined, serene Gupta Buddha with elaborated floral elements in the halo.

statement_analysis.statement: The Sarnath Gupta Buddha and the Mathura Gupta Buddha are stylistically indistinguishable, representing a unified 'Gupta imperial style' that erased all regional differences between the two centers.
statement_analysis.reason: Despite both being Gupta-period schools, Sarnath and Mathura retain distinct regional styles — most visibly in drapery (Sarnath's plain robe vs. Mathura's string-fold), halo design (Sarnath's foliage vs. Mathura's geometric), and material (Chunar vs. Sikri sandstone).

statement_analysis.statement: Both the Mathura and Gandhara schools reached their artistic peak under Kushana patronage, and both declined simultaneously following the fall of the Kushana Empire in the 3rd century CE.
statement_analysis.reason: While both schools flourished under Kushana patronage, they did not decline simultaneously. Mathura continued its tradition through the Gupta period (4th–6th CE) and beyond; the Gandhara school's trajectory was different, but Mathura's is not simply 'post-Kushana decline' — it had a major second florescence under the Guptas.

en.strong_distractor: a — Statement 1 is clearly correct, and students looking for incorrect statements will not select it. But students uncertain about whether Gupta halos at Mathura had 'floral motifs' (versus purely geometric) may incorrectly mark Statement 1 as not correct.
elimination_logic: Statement 1: The Kushana-to-Gupta transition at Mathura involving increased serenity and floral halo elements is correctly described — this is correct, do NOT select.

Statement 2: 'Stylistically indistinguishable' and 'erased all regional differences' are both wrong — Sarnath and Mathura retain distinct drapery, halo, and material differences even in the Gupta period.
Statement 3: The claim that both schools 'declined simultaneously after Kushana fall' is wrong — Mathura had a major Gupta-period florescence after the Kushana era, not a decline.
Both statements 2 and 3 are NOT correct → option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses the conflation technique — merging the distinct Sarnath and Mathura regional styles into a single 'unified Gupta imperial style.' Students who know both are 'Gupta-period schools' may not immediately challenge the 'indistinguishable' claim without precise knowledge of the halo-drapery-material differences. Statement 3 compounds this with a temporal-swap: Mathura's post-Kushana trajectory involved a GUPTA FLORESCENCE, not a simultaneous decline with Gandhara. These two errors together test whether students can hold the distinct trajectories of multiple schools in mind simultaneously.
en.final_explanation:
The Gupta period represents both the maturation of Mathura's tradition and a phase where its distinctiveness from Sarnath must be carefully maintained.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The Gupta-period Mathura Buddha shows clear stylistic evolution from the Kushana phase — the robust physicality gives way to serene spirituality, drapery becomes more refined, and the halo incorporates floral elements alongside its characteristic geometric patterns. This transition is well-documented.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Despite both being Gupta-period products, Sarnath and Mathura are NOT stylistically indistinguishable. Three clear markers persist: (i) drapery — Sarnath's unmodeled plain robe vs. Mathura's string-fold; (ii) halo — Sarnath's foliage-and-figures vs. Mathura's geometric; (iii) material — Chunar sandstone vs. Sikri red sandstone. The 'unified Gupta style' claim is a conflation error.
• Statement 3 — Incorrect: Mathura's post-Kushana history was one of renewal under Gupta patronage, not simultaneous decline with Gandhara. The Gupta period (4th–6th century CE) was Mathura's second major florescence. Gandhara's trajectory (affected by different political dynamics in the northwest) was distinct from Mathura's.

Value Addition:
• The Gupta empire's artistic patronage was not monolithic — it supported regional schools (Mathura, Sarnath, Ajanta) that retained distinct characters.
• The Gandhara school's decline is associated with the Sasanian Persian pressure from the west and the Huna invasions from the north — different from Mathura's pressures.
• Post-Gupta Mathura shows a third phase: increasing ornamentation, greater rigidity, absorption into the emerging Hindu temple sculpture tradition.

• गंधार स्कूल का पतन पश्चिम से सासानी फारसी दबाव और उत्तर से हूण आक्रमणों से जुड़ा था — जो मथुरा के दबावों से भिन्न था।
• गुप्त काल के बाद मथुरा में तीसरा चरण दिखता है: सजावट में वृद्धि, कठोरता, और उभरते हिंदू मंदिर मूर्तिकला परंपरा में समावेशन।
